documentary_basis: VALIDATOR_INVOCATION_MATRIX.json records four supported invocation locations, each at PASS 23/23 with exit code 0.
The four recorded locations are package root, nested review-attempt directory, external private temporary directory, and detached clean-copy external private temporary directory.
STAGE2A_VALIDATION_COMMAND_REGISTER.json and STAGE2A_TEST_CONTROL_REGISTER.json bind the root-resolution control to named commands, tests, source evidence, and the packaged validator hash.
STAGE2A_FINDING_TO_REMEDIATION_MATRIX.json maps the finding to exact requirement, remediation, test, and evidence artifact identities.

STAGE2A_REQUIREMENT_TRACEABILITY_MATRIX.json provides named controls, source evidence identifiers, implementation artifacts, test identifiers, and output evidence for requirements 003, 004, 006, and 009.
STAGE2A_TEST_CONTROL_REGISTER.json and the traceability contract provide executable identities rather than generic category-only mappings.
The frozen foundation validation records a measurable startup inventory of attempted=3, succeeded=2, failed=1, skipped=1, timed_out=0, and unavailable=0, with arithmetic_valid=true.

Four startup-attempt records have unique attempt identifiers, UTC start and end values, and exactly one terminal state: interrupted failpoint failed, cold full-app succeeded, foundation profile skipped as not selected, and rollback restart succeeded.
The provider event ledger contains 11 process-bound, hash-chained records with provider, boundary, configuration, source, reason, attempt, terminal-state, UTC, PID/PGID, and launch-nonce-hash fields.
EVIDENCE_REUSE_AND_RERUN_REGISTER.json classifies predecessor evidence as corroborative only and records a current-candidate lifecycle rerun as PASS 16/16.

EVIDENCE_CAPTURE_VALIDATION.json records PASS and rejects contradictory exit semantics, over-redaction, reverse chronology, sensitive-value retention, stream-hash mismatch, unexpected placeholders, and weak substring matching while preserving required meaning and near-miss values.
EXECUTION_EVIDENCE_SCHEMA.json requires documented evidence classification, redaction status, redaction metadata, and EXECUTION_NOT_AUTHORIZED status.

The packaged pass-evidence record contains projector and normalization versions, before/after projection hashes, sensitive and placeholder counts, exact-line matches, semantic-preservation status, stream hashes, and a record-content hash.

The frozen startup identity evidence records PID, PPID, PGID, command and command hashes, executable path, working directory, controlled port, launch-nonce hash, and identity timestamp for both MongoDB and API processes.

The controlled-shutdown report cross-checks identities, reports listener matches, records both processes STOPPED, confirms both ports closed and PID files absent, and records that no force action was required.
The orchestration contract and shutdown records state fail-closed behavior: identity conflicts prevent signaling or termination rather than permitting action against an unverified process.

limitations: This report is a document-based challenge review. Its conclusions rely only on the frozen archive records and existing validation and test reports; no execution result from this reviewer is used as closure evidence.

The recorded validator, unit-control, lifecycle, evidence, process, and provider results were reconciled for specificity and internal documentary consistency, but were not promoted here as independently rerun or externally assured results.
No runtime behavior, live network behavior, service startup, data alteration, or security or mutation scenario forms part of this review disposition.
The five recommendations are technical closure recommendations only. They do not formally close their findings, authorize execution, close F0001, or establish external assurance.

The runtime agent-type selector remains an explicit, separate, open blocking limitation. Default execution readiness therefore remains blocked even though the five package-control records support closure recommendation.
